Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Let $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with complex multiplication, the subspace topology and the usual smooth circle structure. A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, a smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ exists with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. Different lifts differ locally by an integer multiple of $2\pi$, so their differentials agree and this compatibility condition is independent of the lift. Equivalently, with the globally defined real one-form $\lambda(g)=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ on each overlap, the condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The circle is a smooth Lie group and in particular a topological group: multiplication is the restriction of continuous complex multiplication and inversion is complex conjugation. A right principal $U(1)$-bundle has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts; those charts make the action free and transitive on each fibre, as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies
$\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_{s=0}=-mc\,L'(0)$, so within this class of curves
and variations $\gamma$ is stationary for $S_p$ if and only if
$D_t\gamma'=0$, i.e. if and only if $\gamma$ is a geodesic in its proper-time
parameter ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

The gauge variation is $\alpha=d\chi$ together with the associated matter-field gauge variation, whose action contribution vanishes by [A1]. Gauge invariance and the stated first variation give $0=\delta_\chi S_m= rac1c\int_M j^a

abla_aj^a$; the first term integrates to zero by [F6], because $\operatorname{supp}(\chi j)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\chi$ is compact inside the chosen chart. If $
abla_aj^a$ were nonzero at a point, continuity and a nonnegative compact bump supported where it has fixed sign, whose existence is part of [F6], would contradict the resulting integral identity for all $\chi$. Since the ball and its tests are arbitrary, $
abla_aj^a=0$ at every point of $M$.

Let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field compactly supported inside an arbitrary positively oriented coordinate ball, and use its local flow from [F4] together with the induced horizontal lift to $P$. In a local trivialization with potential $A_a$, the ordinary pullback variation is $(\mathcal L_\xi A)_a=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b=\xi^bF_{ba}+\partial_a(\xi^bA_b)$. The last term is an infinitesimal gauge variation; the horizontal lift removes it. Thus the connection variation is $\alpha_a=\xi^bF_{ba}$. Since $F$ is global by [F2], this formula agrees on overlaps and defines the required global connection variation.

By [F5], the metric derivative along the same local flow has inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=-(
abla^a\xi^b+
abla^b\xi^a)$. Simultaneous diffeomorphism invariance, the on-shell matter condition [A1], and the first-variation formula therefore give $0= rac1c\int_M\left(T^m_{ab}
abla^a\xi^b+j^a\xi^bF_{ba}ight)\mathrm{vol}_g$, where symmetry of $T^m$ combines its two metric-variation terms.

The product rule gives $T^m_{ab}
abla^a\xi^b=
abla^a(T^m_{ab}\xi^b)-(
abla^aT^m_{ab})\xi^b$. The vector field $W^a=(T^m)^a{}_b\xi^b$ is compactly supported inside the chosen chart, so its divergence integrates to zero by [F6], so step 2.1 becomes $\int_M(-
abla^aT^m_{ab}+F_{ba}j^a)\xi^b\,\mathrm{vol}_g=0$ for every vector test $\xi$ compactly supported inside that ball. The ball was arbitrary; [F6] therefore makes the smooth covector coefficient vanish pointwise throughout $M$. Relabeling the contracted index and raising $b$ yields $

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies
$\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_{s=0}=-mc\,L'(0)$, so within this class of curves
and variations $\gamma$ is stationary for $S_p$ if and only if
$D_t\gamma'=0$, i.e. if and only if $\gamma$ is a geodesic in its proper-time
parameter ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold, let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $(U,x)$ be any smooth
chart, with indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$. Write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$,
let $(g^{ab})$ be the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$, and define the strictly
positive chart weight $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$. These are local
matrix constructions; no signature, time orientation or orientation is assumed.
A continuous covariant tensor field means a family of bilinear forms whose
chart components are continuous; smooth means that they are $C^\infty$.
For a covector or vector field the same regularity convention applies to its
components in the coordinate dual basis or coordinate basis, respectively.
Let $F$ be a
continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$. Suppose that for every
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $q$ on $M$ whose support is a
compact subset of $U$,

$$\int_U F_{ab}(x)\,q^{ab}(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0,$$

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Write $;e$ for the induced
covariant derivative and raise indices with $g^{-1}$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Second Bianchi identity.** For all indices $a,b,c,d,e$,
$$R^a{}_{bcd;e}+R^a{}_{bde;c}+R^a{}_{bec;d}=0,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad R_{abcd;e}+R_{abde;c}+R_{abec;d}=0 .$$
Equivalently, the antisymmetrization over the last three slots vanishes:
$R^a{}_{b[cd;e]}=0$.

**(b) Contracted identities.** $\nabla^a\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
=\tfrac12\nabla_bS$, and consequently
$$\nabla^aG_{ab}=0\qquad\text{for every }b,$$
where $\nabla^aG_{ab}:=g^{ae}\nabla_eG_{ab}$. The conclusion is the vanishing
of the contracted divergence for each second index; it does not assert that
all components $\nabla_cG_{ab}$ vanish.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For an oriented smooth manifold $M^n$, possibly with boundary, and $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$, choose a smooth partition $(\rho_i)$ subordinate to connected interior or boundary charts $(U_i,\phi_i)$. For $n\geq1$ set
$$\int_M\omega=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\rho_i\omega).$$
Each product has compact support in its chart and only finitely many are nonzero, by [[lem-a-locally-finite-sum-is-finite-near-the-compact-support-of-a-form]]. For $n=0$ set
$$\int_M\omega=\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p).$$
$\Lambda^0T_p^*M\cong\mathbb R$ has two orientations; define $\varepsilon(p)=+1$ when $1$ is positive in the chosen orientation and $\varepsilon(p)=-1$ when $-1$ is positive.
A zero-manifold is discrete; the singleton open cover of a compact subset has a finite subcover. Thus this sum too is finite. Empty support or empty $M$ gives zero. Independence of the choices is discharged by [[thm-global-form-integration-is-independent-of-the-atlas-partition-and-refinement]].

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The compact-support integral on an oriented manifold is independent of the chart cover, coordinate maps, subordinate partition, and refinement. If $U\subset M$ is open and contains $\operatorname{supp}\omega$, with its restricted orientation, then $\int_U\omega|_U=\int_M\omega$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

derivations.claim: For a family in [A1], the top form $\omega_s=(R(g(s))-2\Lambda)\mathrm{vol}_{g(s)}-(R(g)-2\Lambda)\mathrm{vol}_g$ is supported in the common compact $K$. Define its relative action by [F6], even if the separate background integrals diverge. Fix a subordinate partition independently of $s$; only finitely many terms meet $K$, and each has compact support inside its chart. The uniform difference-quotient argument in the Maxwell supplier [F2] differentiates this finite sum. Clause (d) of [F1] gives its derivative density locally, and $\delta(-2\Lambda\mathrm{vol}_g)=\Lambda g_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$. The field $V$ is global because $\delta\Gamma$ is a tensor, and is supported in $K$. The compact divergence argument in [F2] now gives $\int_M\nabla_aV^a\mathrm{vol}_g=0$: apply chart FTC to each $\rho_iV$ and sum, with $\sum_i d\rho_i=0$ near $K$. Thus no single chart or enclosing finite singular chain is presumed. Multiplication by $c^3/(16\pi G_N)$ yields $\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$, as claimed.
Add [F2] and [F3]. Since $\frac{1}{2c}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}$, the total variation is exactly the expression in the Statement with $\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4$.

If the action is stationary for every compactly supported $q^{ab}$, step 2.1 implies that the continuous symmetric coefficient $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})$ pairs to zero with every such $q$. Because $c,G_N>0$, its prefactor is nonzero; [F4] therefore gives the displayed field equation pointwise.

Conversely, if the displayed field equation holds pointwise, the coefficient in step 2.1 is zero everywhere, so its integral vanishes for every compactly supported $q$. This proves stationarity and the equivalence.

Take the covariant divergence of the field equation in step 3.1. By [F5], $
abla^aG_{ab}=0$ and $
abla^a(\Lambda g_{ab})=\Lambda
abla^ag_{ab}=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. Since $\kappa_E>0$, division gives $
abla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$. No PDE existence follows from this necessary compatibility identity.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

citations.quote: Let $G$ be a topological group, as in [[def-topological-group]], with identity $1$. A **right principal $G$-bundle** is a continuous map $\pi:P\to B$ with a continuous right action $(p,g)\mapsto pg$, satisfying $p1=p$, $(pg)h=p(gh)$ and $\pi(pg)=\pi(p)$, together with equivariant bundle charts $\theta_i:\pi^{-1}(U_i)\cong U_i\times G$ over an open cover. Equivariance means $\theta_i(pg)=(b,ag)$ whenever $\theta_i(p)=(b,a)$. Charts use ordinary products as in [[def-locally-trivial-fiber-bundle]].

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Let $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with complex multiplication, the subspace topology and the usual smooth circle structure. A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, a smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ exists with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. Different lifts differ locally by an integer multiple of $2\pi$, so their differentials agree and this compatibility condition is independent of the lift. Equivalently, with the globally defined real one-form $\lambda(g)=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ on each overlap, the condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The circle is a smooth Lie group and in particular a topological group: multiplication is the restriction of continuous complex multiplication and inversion is complex conjugation. A right principal $U(1)$-bundle has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts; those charts make the action free and transitive on each fibre, as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts.

The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. $$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

For $a>0$, integer $m$ and integer $n\ge1$, define the rational regime by

$$
a^{m/n}:=(a^{1/n})^m,
$$

where $a^{1/n}$ is the unique positive root of $s^n=a$ in [[thm-nth-roots-exist]], and integer powers include reciprocals for negative $m$. This is [[def-rational-power]]; [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]] proves independence of the fraction representative and [[lem-rational-power-laws]] gives the rational exponent laws. The supplementary convention is $0^r=0$ for rational $r>0$; $0^0$ and negative powers of zero remain undefined.

The separate real regime is [[def-real-power]]: for $a>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R$, $a^x=\exp(x\log a)$, with the laws of [[thm-real-power-laws]]. For $x>0$ set $0^x=0$; no arbitrary real power is assigned to a negative base. The real-power laws are supplied by that theorem, not inferred from the rational root formula. Use the real-number structure of [[def-real-numbers]].

In particular $s(q)=q^{1/2}$ for $q>0$ is the unique positive solution of $s(q)^2=q$. Its smoothness and derivative are a separate well-definedness result, not an assumption about fractional notation.

Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff second-countable manifold **without boundary**, in the sense of [[def-smooth-manifold]]. Let $g$ be a positive definite smooth Riemannian metric as in [[def-riemannian-metric-symmetric-cotangent-connection-and-covariant-hessian]]. Use the Levi-Civita connection of [[def-levi-civita-connection]] with the existence and coordinate formula supplied by [[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]; in coordinates it has coefficients $\Gamma^k_{ij}=\frac12g^{kl}(\partial_i g_{jl}+\partial_j g_{il}-\partial_l g_{ij})$. A parametrized affine geodesic is a smooth curve $\gamma:J\to M$ on an interval with nonempty interior satisfying $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma=0$, equivalently $\ddot\gamma^k+\Gamma^k_{ij}(\gamma)\dot\gamma^i\dot\gamma^j=0$, where covariant differentiation along the curve is defined by [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]; the coordinate equation is the expansion of that derivative in a coordinate basis. Its maximal domain is an interval on which it cannot be extended with the same affine parameter as a solution. **Two-sided geodesic completeness** means that every maximal affine geodesic is defined on all of $\mathbb R$.

Independently, for a real metric $d$ in [[def-metric-space]], a sequence $(x_n)$ is Cauchy when for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N$ with $d(x_m,x_n)<\varepsilon$ whenever $m,n\ge N$. It converges to $x$ when for every $\varepsilon>0$ eventually $d(x_n,x)<\varepsilon$. **Metric completeness** means that every Cauchy sequence converges in the given metric space. In a Riemannian application the metric must be the distance induced by $g$ on a connected component: the infimum of lengths $\int\sqrt{g(\dot\alpha,\dot\alpha)}\,dt$ over piecewise-$C^1$ connecting curves. Its definition and finite metric property are supplied by [[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]] and [[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]. Specify that induced metric, rather than an arbitrary compatible metric. Distinct components are treated separately; no infinite distance is inserted into a real metric.

These are different completeness conditions. Their equivalence is a Hopf–Rinow theorem requiring its own hypotheses and proof; it is not part of this definition. In particular, a Lorentzian metric is not a positive definite distance, and this convention supplies no Lorentzian Hopf–Rinow implication.

The boundaryless restriction matters: the Euclidean interval $[0,1]$ is metrically complete, while the curve $\gamma(t)=1/2+t$ stays inside it only for $-1/2\le t\le1/2$ and cannot be continued there as a two-sided affine geodesic with velocity $1$. Completeness of this interval follows because a real Cauchy sequence converges in $\mathbb R$ by [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]] and its limit remains between $0$ and $1$. This boundary example explains the domain restriction; it is not an instance of the boundaryless equivalence.

Use the first-order language of [[def-language-of-set-theory]]: all quantified objects are sets, and a **definable class** $\{x:\varphi(x,p)\}$ abbreviates a formula with set parameters $p$. It is not a new set or a domain for unrestricted quantification. Work with the usual set axioms, in particular [[def-axiom-of-power-set]] and [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]], and the ordered pairs, products and functions of [[def-ordered-pair]], [[def-cartesian-product]] and [[def-function]]. The power-set axiom supplies a collecting set; Separation trims it to exactly $\mathcal P(X)=\{Y:Y\subseteq X\}$.

A **small category** has a set $O$ of objects, a set $A$ of arrows, source and target functions $s,t:A\to O$, an identity function $e:O\to A$, and a composition function on the set $\{(a,b)\in A\times A:s(a)=t(b)\}$, where $ab$ denotes $a\circ b$ and the laws are $s(e(x))=t(e(x))=x$, $s(ab)=s(b)$, $t(ab)=t(a)$, $e(t(a))a=a=ae(s(a))$, and $(ab)c=a(bc)$ whenever the displayed compositions are defined. It is **locally small** when each specified hom-collection is a set. A definable large category is a schema of formulas for its objects, arrows and operations, with those laws asserted as formulas; it is not a set of all objects or a category of all large categories. No Grothendieck universe is assumed.

All indexed families in the local bundle construction have a supplied set index $I$. If $U_i\subseteq M$ and $G$ is a set, their tagged disjoint union is the subset $D=\{(i,x,z)\in I\times M\times G:x\in U_i\}$, formed by Separation. Given a set equivalence relation $E\subseteq D\times D$, each class $[u]_E=\{v\in D:(u,v)\in E\}$ is a subset of $D$, and the quotient is the set

$$
D/E=\{C\in\mathcal P(D):\exists u\in D\ \forall v\in D\ (v\in C\iff(u,v)\in E)\}.
$$

Thus the quotient is obtained by Separation in $\mathcal P(D)$, without choosing representatives. Transition-map graphs and connection data are subsets of specified finite products and power sets, not arbitrary proper-class objects.

For the Cauchy-development coding application, fix a set manifold $\Sigma$ and the tensor-bundle total spaces over $\Sigma\times\mathbb R$. A code consists of an open set $D\subseteq\Sigma\times\mathbb R$, graphs of a metric and a two-form on $D$ inside those fixed total spaces, a time orientation, and a fixed initial embedding. All of its coordinates belong to fixed products and power sets. Separation selects the tuples satisfying the specified smoothness, Lorentzian, field-equation and initial-data formulas. Hence these codes form a set. This size assertion does not prove field-equation existence, maximality or uniqueness, and makes no proper-class representative choice.
